skill_outcomes.outcome_description: Understand the role and scope of government intervention in a market economy.
Comprehend the four fundamental roles of government: resource allocation, income redistribution, macroeconomic stability, and national representation on international forums.
Recognize the limitations of government intervention in a market economy.
Understand the research object, content, and methods of the course.
Analyze different types of market failures and the role of government intervention.
Understand the benefits of public choice and compare principles of public choice within a direct democratic mechanism.
Systematically understand various policy tools used by governments to intervene in market economies.
Analyze social equity issues in income distribution and their relationship with economic efficiency.
Measure poverty and its impact on society.
Develop independent learning and research skills to enhance professional expertise and adapt to dynamic work environments.
Gain ethical awareness and professional responsibility in participating in the formulation, monitoring, and evaluation of government policies.
